messages:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel-selection canary (yesterday) we're seeing ~12% p95 decode latency increase on small requests. Noticed it when running the microburst workload.
jon: I see that in staging traces too. p95 spikes line up with microbatching enabled + a jump in kv cache evictions.
tanvi: Can you paste the perf flame or the perf counters?
maria: quick snippet from the flame (staged):
```
service.request_parse 1.1ms
host.tokenize 1.3ms
kernel.select_fp16 0.9ms
kernel.exec_fp16 3.0ms
kv_cache.lookup 0.6ms (misses up 30%)
stream.writev 0.4ms (many tiny writes)
```
jon: Interesting — kernel.select is bouncing between two kernels for seq_len ~48-80. That churn + kvcache misses explains CPU churn and more tiny grpc frames.
alex: Also seeing lots of 1-2 token grpc frames -> writev thrash on the sidecar. Wire-level sample: 80% of frames are <96 bytes.
maria: Related change: host preproc started doing per-request tokenization tasks (no shared tokenizer pool) for small requests to simplify isolation. That adds ~1.2ms CPU per request at peak.
tanvi: So multiple contributors: kernel swap noise, kvcache eviction rate increase, microbatching heuristics producing smaller batch sizes, and small-write overhead on grpc http2.
jon: Quick experiments we can try: 1) bump microbatch window from 4ms -> 8ms to allow slightly larger batches; 2) pin kernel selection for seq_len < 96 to the stable kernel; 3) increase kv cache residency for recent keys; 4) enable write coalescing in the streaming shim to reduce writev count.
maria: Measured tradeoffs: increasing window to 8ms reduced CPU by ~18% on the microburst test (fewer kernel context switches) but added ~2ms median latency on sub-50 token requests. p95 improved significantly.
jon: For KV cache, if eviction_rate drops the backend I/O falls and kv lookup latency stabilizes. We should be conservative with TTLs: try +2x residency first.
alex: Coalescing write path: cheap to implement in the shim — coalesce up to N bytes or until finish event. Risk: adds a tiny headroom delay. In a test we batched 3 small frames into one write and reduced syscall count by 70%.
tanvi: Also check gRPC Nagle-like behavior on http2 small writes. Might be tuning on the socket level and writev behaviour.
perf-bot: Created perf run comparing baseline vs canary: run_id=6001213500 — results will attach when ready.
maria: Proposal for next steps (owners): A) run canary with microbatch window=8ms in staging (owner: jon) B) enable shim write coalescing behind feature flag in sidecar (owner: tanvi) C) bump kv cache TTL (owner: jon) D) pin short-seq kernel to stable selection for 72h canary (owner: maria) E) add metrics: kv_eviction_rate, small_write_count, kernel_switch_rate (owner: tanvi)
jon: I'll open PRs for batching window + kvcache TTL and add the perf gate.
tanvi: I'll add instrumentation in the streaming shim and a unit test for coalescing behavior.
alex: I'll collect wire stats and a tiny tcpdump sample for the tiny frames to confirm coalescing impact.
maria: Timeline: run the staging canary today, collect 6h of traces, reconvene tomorrow morning with perf-bot numbers. If p95 improves we'll roll the batching window + write coalescing to canary traffic.
jon: sounds good. I'll also add a temporary metric alert if kernel_switch_rate > 5/s per host.
tanvi: FYI — coalescing flag will be opt-in so we can ramp.
maria: Assigning owners in the checklist above. Will post follow-up with perf-bot outputs. Thanks all.
jon: :thumbsup:
